title: A table, a cubic and a model type justified

stimulus.title: Values of f, and the function g
stimulus.html:
The table gives values of the increasing function ff at selected values of xx. The function gg is given by g(x)=x3−6x2+9x+2g(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 2.
Selected values of the function f
xx02468
f(x)f(x)34.87.6812.28819.6608

parts.label: A(i)
parts.prompt: Find the average rate of change of ff over the interval 0≤x≤40 \le x \le 4 and over the interval 4≤x≤84 \le x \le 8.

rubric.point: Both values: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.17</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.17</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 4]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.9952</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.9952</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[4, 8]</annotation></semantics></math>, with the difference quotients
accept: values correct to three decimal places (2.995)

parts.sample: On <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 4]</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{f(4) - f(0)}{4 - 0}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>7.68</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{7.68 - 3}{4}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1.17</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1.17</annotation></semantics></math>. On <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[4, 8]</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{f(8) - f(4)}{8 - 4}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>19.6608</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>7.68</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{19.6608 - 7.68}{4}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2.9952</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2.9952</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: Based on the results of part A(i), is the graph of ff concave up or concave down on 0≤x≤80 \le x \le 8? Give a reason for your answer.

rubric.point: Concave up, with a reason: the average rates of change over consecutive equal-length intervals increase
accept: "concave up, because the average rate of change on [4, 8], 2.9952, is greater than on [0, 4], 1.17, and the intervals have equal length"
"the rate of change of f is increasing"

parts.sample: Concave up. Over the consecutive intervals <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 4]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[4, 8]</annotation></semantics></math>, which have equal length, the average rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> increases from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.17</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.17</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.9952</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.9952</annotation></semantics></math>, so the rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is increasing.

parts.label: B(i)
parts.prompt: Solve g(x)=4g(x) = 4 for all values of xx. Give your answers correct to three decimal places where needed.

rubric.point: All three solutions and no others: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.268</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0.268</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3.732</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 3.732</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: Graph <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = g(x)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 4</annotation></semantics></math> and find every intersection (widen the window to be sure there are no more; a cubic has at most three): <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.268</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0.268</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3.732</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 3.732</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: B(ii)
parts.prompt: Express the end behavior of gg, as xx decreases without bound and as xx increases without bound, using the mathematical notation of limits.

rubric.point: Both limits correct in limit notation: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to -\infty} g(x) = -\infty</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to \infty} g(x) = \infty</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to -\infty} g(x) = -\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to \infty} g(x) = \infty</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: The leading term is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^3</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to -\infty} g(x) = -\infty</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to \infty} g(x) = \infty</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: C(i)
parts.prompt: Is a linear function or an exponential function a better model for the values in the table? Justify your answer, using the input and output values in the table.

rubric.point: Exponential, with both halves: the input values change by equal amounts (<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>) and the output values change proportionally (constant ratio <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.6</annotation></semantics></math>)
accept: "exponential: over equal-length input intervals of 2, the outputs have a constant ratio, 4.8/3 = 7.68/4.8 = 12.288/7.68 = 19.6608/12.288 = 1.6"
no point if either the equal-length input intervals or the proportional outputs (with values) is missing

parts.sample: Exponential. The inputs increase by equal amounts of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>, and over each of these intervals the outputs are multiplied by the same factor: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>4.8</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{4.8}{3}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>7.68</mn><mn>4.8</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{7.68}{4.8}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>12.288</mn><mn>7.68</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{12.288}{7.68}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>19.6608</mn><mn>12.288</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{19.6608}{12.288}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1.6</annotation></semantics></math>. The differences (<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.8</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.88</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.88</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4.608</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.608</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>7.3728</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.3728</annotation></semantics></math>) are not constant, so a linear function does not fit.

parts.label: C(ii)
parts.prompt: Write an expression for an exponential function that matches every value in the table.

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.6</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = 3(1.6)^{x/2}</annotation></semantics></math> or an equivalent form
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.264911</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3(1.264911...)^x</annotation></semantics></math> with the base correct to three decimal places

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(0) = 3</annotation></semantics></math> and the outputs are multiplied by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.6</annotation></semantics></math> every <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> units, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.6</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = 3(1.6)^{x/2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
